input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer (fifteen percent of annual Fees for each week of delay), which breaches the preferred position of no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer and is punitive in scale. Our redline is now confined to that defect: we delete the liquidated-damages amount and substitute simple interest capped at one percent per month (or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, a defined term at Section 1.2) as Vendor's sole remedy, leaving the existing ten-day trigger and the Section 7.3 dispute-withholding mechanics untouched. No early-termination fee exists elsewhere (Section 9.4 limits Customer to accrued Fees), so the three-month fallback cap is unnecessary; service credits payable to us and the mutual cap in Section 21 raise no issue.

ops.oldText: Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
ops.newText: Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest on the overdue amount at the lesser of one percent per month or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, accruing from the due date until payment.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We deleted the liquidated damages of fifteen percent of annual Fees per week and replaced it with simple late-payment interest capped at one percent per month (or the legal maximum) as Vendor's sole remedy, because our playbook does not accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer. The ten-day trigger and the dispute mechanics in Section 7.3 are unchanged.
proposal.summary: Replace Customer-payable liquidated damages in 7.7 with simple late-payment interest as Vendor's sole remedy; timing untouched.
